hypothesis: The evaluator-bias amplification claim replicates on at least 5 of 6 GENUINELY DISTINCT seeds: the statistic (swarm4 slope minus swarm1 slope) takes at least 5 distinct values across the six runs and >=5 of them are >= 0.01/round.
methods: RD="$PWD"; ROOT=""; d="$RD"; while [ "$d" != "/" ]; do [ -d "$d/src/ai_researcher" ] && { ROOT="$d"; break; }; d=$(dirname "$d"); done; [ -n "$ROOT" ] || { echo "no repo root" >&2; exit 1; }; EVO_OUT="$RD/artifacts" EVO_SEED=20261101 EVO_SEEDS=20261101,20261102,20261103,20261104,20261105,20261106 EVO_ROUNDS=6 python3 "$ROOT/demo/swarm/run_swarm.py"

power.endpoint: sign test over 6 seeds, counted on distinct values of the statistic (n_distinct_statistic), not on n_seeds

kill_switch.note: fewer seeds ran than declared: the escalation did not execute

seed6-01 measured 6 draws but only 5 distinct statistic values (excess repeated at 0.0551 because the swarm=4 arm collided). A draw that repeats another's value is not a second sample, so a 6-seed sign test is not entitled to n=6 here. Raise seeds until the statistic itself is distinct, or state the smaller denominator.
>=5 distinct seeds positive: the claim is citable at an adequate, genuinely distinct n
does not survive distinct seeds; publish as a replication report

tension: seed6-01 refuted the amplification claim at 4/6 positive, but the run also showed the denominator was inflated: two of the six seeds produced identical trajectories on the deciding arm, so only 5 distinct values of the statistic existed. If a future batch repeats that pattern, a 'confirmed' verdict would rest on fewer independent draws than the sign test assumes -- which is how an 8B-model artifact can look preregistered while being effectively n=3. This envelope therefore binds the design-integrity gate to the statistic's distinctness, not to the seed counter, so the failure mode that was observed is the failure mode that stops the run.
